body.id: Hangul punya 10 vokal dasar. Garis panjangnya berdiri │ atau berbaring ─.
body.en: Hangul has 10 basic vowels. The long line stands │ or lies down ─.

body.id: Vokal tanpa konsonan ditemani ㅇ yang diam: ㅏ ditulis 아 (a).
body.en: A vowel with no consonant gets a silent ㅇ: ㅏ is written 아 (a).

body.id: Ke orang dewasa, bilang 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo). Ke teman, cukup 안녕 (annyeong).
body.en: To grown-ups, say 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo). To friends, just 안녕 (annyeong).

body.id: Konsonan duduk di kiri atau di atas vokal: 가 (ga), 고 (go).
body.en: A consonant sits left of or above the vowel: 가 (ga), 고 (go).

body.id: Menghitung benda dan umur: 하나 (hana), 둘 (dul), 셋 (set) …
body.en: Counting things and age: 하나 (hana), 둘 (dul), 셋 (set) …

body.id: Uang dan nomor telepon: 일 (il), 이 (i), 삼 (sam) …
body.en: Money and phone numbers: 일 (il), 이 (i), 삼 (sam) …

body.id: Huruf ketiga duduk di bawah. Namanya 받침 (batchim): 공 (gong), 산 (san).
body.en: A third letter sits at the bottom. It's called 받침 (batchim): 공 (gong), 산 (san).

body.id: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ diucapkan dengan hembusan napas: 카 (ka).
body.en: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ come with a puff of air: 카 (ka).

body.id: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ diucapkan tegang, tanpa hembusan: 까 (kka).
body.en: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are said tight, with no puff: 까 (kka).

body.id: 엄마 (eomma) ibu, 아빠 (appa) ayah, 할머니 (halmeoni) nenek, 할아버지 (harabeoji) kakek.
body.en: 엄마 (eomma) mum, 아빠 (appa) dad, 할머니 (halmeoni) grandma, 할아버지 (harabeoji) grandpa.

body.id: Anak perempuan memanggil kakaknya 언니 (eonni) dan 오빠 (oppa).
body.en: A girl calls her older sister 언니 (eonni) and her older brother 오빠 (oppa).

body.id: Anak laki-laki memanggil kakaknya 누나 (nuna) dan 형 (hyeong).
body.en: A boy calls his older sister 누나 (nuna) and his older brother 형 (hyeong).

body.id: Mau sesuatu? Sebut bendanya, lalu 주세요 (juseyo): 물 주세요 (mul juseyo).
body.en: Want something? Say the thing, then 주세요 (juseyo): 물 주세요 (mul juseyo).

body.id: Sebelum makan, orang Korea bilang 잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida).
body.en: Before eating, Koreans say 잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida).

body.id: Untuk bilang "Ini ___", tambahkan 예요 (yeyo) atau 이에요 (ieyo).
body.en: To say "It's a ___", add 예요 (yeyo) or 이에요 (ieyo).

body.id: Tanpa 받침: 고양이예요 (goyangiyeyo). Ada 받침: 공이에요 (gongieyo).
body.en: No batchim: 고양이예요 (goyangiyeyo). With a batchim: 공이에요 (gongieyo).

model_answer.en: ㅏ says a, as in "father".

model_answer.id: ㅓ dibaca eo: mulut terbuka, bibir tidak bulat.
model_answer.en: ㅓ says eo: mouth open, lips not rounded.

model_answer.id: ㅜ dibaca u, seperti u di "buku".
model_answer.en: ㅜ says u, as in "zoo".

model_answer.id: ㅣ dibaca i, seperti i di "ikan".
model_answer.en: ㅣ says i, as in "see".

model_answer.id: Berdiri: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ. Berbaring: ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ.

model_answer.id: ㅇ diam di depan vokal: 아 (a). Di bawah, bunyinya ng: 공 (gong).

model_answer.en: 아 + 이 = 아이 (ai), child.

model_answer.id: Tambah satu garis, tambah bunyi y: ㅑ dibaca ya.
model_answer.en: One more stroke adds a y: ㅑ says ya.

model_answer.id: ㅕ dibaca yeo.
model_answer.en: ㅕ says yeo.

model_answer.id: Ke guru, pakai salam sopan: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo).
model_answer.en: To a teacher, use the polite hello: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo).

model_answer.id: ㅛ dibaca yo.
model_answer.en: ㅛ says yo.

model_answer.id: ㅠ dibaca yu.
model_answer.en: ㅠ says yu.

model_answer.id: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida) = terima kasih.
model_answer.en: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida) = thank you.

model_answer.id: Berdiri: ㅑ ㅕ ㅣ. Berbaring: ㅛ ㅠ ㅡ.
model_answer.en: Standing: ㅑ ㅕ ㅣ. Lying down: ㅛ ㅠ ㅡ.

items.source: UNESCO Memory of the World Register, 'Hunminjeongum Manuscript' (inscribed 1997); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hangul'; Korea.net (Korean Culture and Information Service), 'Hangeul Day': 9 October marks the proclamation of 1446.

model_answer.id: Dulu orang Korea menulis dengan huruf Tionghoa yang sulit. Tahun 1443, Raja Sejong membuat hangul supaya semua orang bisa membaca. Setiap 9 Oktober, Korea Selatan merayakan Hari Hangul.
model_answer.en: Long ago, Koreans wrote with hard Chinese characters. In 1443, King Sejong created hangul so that everyone could read. Every 9 October, South Korea celebrates Hangul Day.

items.source: Hunminjeongeum Haerye (1446), chapter Jejahae ('Explanation of the design of the letters'): ㄱ the root of the tongue closing the throat, ㄴ the tongue touching the upper gum, ㅁ the mouth, ㅅ a tooth, ㅇ the throat; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hangul'; National Institute of Korean Language (korean.go.kr).

model_answer.id: Bentuk konsonan meniru mulut kita! ㄱ: pangkal lidah menutup tenggorokan. ㄴ: ujung lidah menyentuh gusi atas. ㅁ: mulut. ㅅ: gigi. ㅇ: tenggorokan.
model_answer.en: Consonant shapes copy your mouth! ㄱ: the back of the tongue closing the throat. ㄴ: the tongue tip touching the upper gum. ㅁ: the mouth. ㅅ: a tooth. ㅇ: the throat.

model_answer.id: ㅋ namanya 키읔 (kieuk): ㄱ + satu garis, k dengan hembusan.

model_answer.id: ㅌ namanya 티읕 (tieut): ㄷ + satu garis, t dengan hembusan.

model_answer.en: That was 카 (ka), with a puff. 가 (ga) is soft, 까 (kka) is tight.
